ACTS.name: Act IV
ACTS.question: What will you do with it?

PAGES.title: Pressed flower
PAGES.text: I went back for the flower that grew where Clover fell. It has her ears, two soft petals that twitch when I hum. I pressed it in this book. Turn the page carefully.

PAGES.title: Walls that ring
PAGES.text: Pip says the Bloom hides rooms behind walls that ring. I struck one today and it answered with a note from the deep song, the one I keep humming. The Bloom has a voice, and it uses it to keep secrets.

PAGES.title: Biscuit digs
PAGES.text: Biscuit has started digging toward the deep at night, the way the wild ones do. Her tether is cut. I watched it fall away. So what is still calling her?

PAGES.title: A map with a hole in it
PAGES.text: Pip's map of Floor 3 has a hole where the boss room should be. She swears she drew it, then the room moved. Boss rooms never move. Something moved it to keep me away from what Biscuit became.

PAGES.title: The camp ledger
PAGES.text: Copied from a ledger in the Abyss camp: 'Day 212 of the Planting. Seed vaults full. The Bloom takes well. Coal for the forge, bread for forty Keepers.' Forty. There were forty of them, and they called it a planting.

PAGES.title: The pumps
PAGES.text: The Old Keepers built pumps to keep the galleries dry. Pumps mean years of work, not a season. This was never a camp. It was a post. They were tending something, the way I tend the garden.

PAGES.title: Three crowns
PAGES.text: Three crowns on a ledge in the Choir dark, set down neatly, like someone took them off to sleep. Not kings' crowns. Gardeners' wreaths, cast in iron so they would last.

PAGES.title: Chimes
PAGES.text: The wind in the Spires blows down, always down, toward the heart. The Old Keepers hung chimes on every ledge so they could find their way back up by sound. They meant to come back up. Most of them did.

PAGES.title: The same shapes
PAGES.text: I have copied the rune line from twelve walls now. Same shapes every time, in the same order. If it really says KEEP IT ASLEEP, then the second shape is E, it comes twice, and the last word starts with the same shape as the second word ends. With patience I can read every wall in the Bloom.

PAGES.title: Medicine for creatures
PAGES.text: Their medicine stores are in the Sump. Every bottle is labeled for creatures, none for people. Either the Keepers never fell sick down here, or they did not think of themselves as anything different.

PAGES.title: The drill
PAGES.text: The Keepers' digging engine has a plate on its side: DIG TO THE HEART. CUT NOTHING. Why build a drill that is forbidden to cut? Unless they only ever meant to listen.

PAGES.title: One body
PAGES.text: Sorrel was right. Down here the roots are warm and they have a pulse, one pulse, in every hall at once. We are not exploring a dungeon. We are walking around inside something that is asleep.

PAGES.title: The scar
PAGES.text: I found it this morning. A thin white line over my heart, like a healed thread. My mother had one. I always thought it was a burn from the forge.

PAGES.title: The third voice
PAGES.text: The song has three voices. Two are old and tired. The third is younger, and it sings the same three notes my grandmother sang over my cradle. A Marrow sang here before me.

PAGES.title: Why I went
PAGES.text: If Keepers carry the thread too, then the Bloom has been calling us home all along. The singers are failing. Someone has to hold the song. It should be someone who belongs to it.

PAGES.title: To you
PAGES.text: If you found this room, you read the walls. Good. The Old Keepers rest here: three chairs, two of them still warm. Mine is the third. Whatever you decide at the Heart, decide it awake. — Ilsa

PAGES.title: After
PAGES.text: A new entry, in Ilsa's hand, on the last page: I can hear the hills again. The roots stopped singing and I did not stop breathing. Thank you for coming down. Thank you for not leaving me there.

WALLS.text: WE ARE THE KEEPERS OF THE ARK
WE PLANTED THE BLOOM BELOW TO HOLD WHAT WAS LEFT
WE SANG SO IT WOULD DREAM
VENOM WED TO LIGHT MAKES AN ECLIPSE
THREE STAYED BELOW TO KEEP THE SONG
BRED TRUE THRICE THE BLOOM LETS GO
A DOOR SLEEPS BESIDE THE HEART
IT IS NOT CRUEL IT IS AFRAID
WAKE IT OR CUT IT FREE OR SING IT HOME

WHISPER.note: Rolled once per room entered, with the visual-only random so seeded raids never shift.

WHISPERS.text: Somewhere behind the walls, a girl laughs. Then nothing.
Your companion stops and turns toward the deep, ears up, listening to something you can't hear.
A voice, very close to your ear: "Not this one. This one goes home."
For one bar, the walls hum the tune from the music box on Ilsa's desk.
The coals whisper numbers as you pass. Forty. Thirty-nine. Thirty-eight.
Under the water, a pump turns over once, as if someone remembered it.
In the dark, three voices take a breath together, and hold it.
A chime rings on a ledge where no wind reaches. It rings upward.
The poison bubbles out half a word, something like "eclipse", then forgets it.
A rune on the wall glows as you pass, the way a word does when you finally understand it.
The floor rises and falls under your feet. Slowly. Asleep.
A voice hoarse from a hundred years of singing: "Are you a Marrow? You walk like one."
Your own chest aches, right where a thread would be.
The Bloom speaks in every voice it has ever kept, all at once: "Stay."
Ilsa, beside you, humming: "It only ever wanted someone to stay. Let's show it what leaving looks like."

MURALS.name: The Gardeners
stages: Faded figures with trowels kneel in a ring around a single seed.
The paint has darkened. The seed has roots now, and forty gardeners stand around it holding hands.
The roots reach the edge of the wall. Three gardeners sit apart from the others, mouths open, singing.
A fourth figure kneels beside the three, with a red braid like Ilsa's. Someone has painted her in fresh.

MURALS.name: The Grey Sky
stages: A grey sky over dead fields and dry riverbeds.
A line of people walks out of the grey fields and into a cave, carrying seed sacks.
Someone, much later, painted over the grey with green. The brush marks are hurried.
Under the green sky, creatures pour out of the cave mouth into the fields.

MURALS.name: Biscuit
stages: A girl and a little Puffcap, side by side, drawn in chalk.
The Puffcap stands alone now, facing the deep. The girl's outline has been rubbed away.
The Puffcap has bloomed into a great mother, roots spreading from her feet.
The great bloom has turned her face toward the light of the hideout.

MURALS.name: The Thread
stages: A red line runs from a creature's chest down into the earth.
Keepers sit at looms, weaving the red lines like cloth.
The red line runs into a human chest too. Someone has scratched at it, trying to remove it.
The line is cut. Both ends glow.

MURALS.name: Three Voices
stages: Three faint open mouths, so worn you could mistake them for knots in the stone.
Three crowned singers, gardeners' wreaths on their heads.
Two singers sleep with their heads bowed. The third chair is empty.
A woman sits in the third chair. Her eyes are open.

MURALS.name: Pip's Map
stages: Pip's chalk map of floors 1 to 3, the boss rooms circled twice.
Five veins fan out below the third floor, each in its own color.
A huge round shape under the veins, marked UNDERHEART with a question mark.
At the very center, a shape like a seed, labeled in Pip's hand: IT WAS ALWAYS A SEED.

MURALS.name: The Keeper's Hand
stages: A handprint in old red clay, older than the hideout.
Forty handprints around it, all different sizes.
Each handprint has a thin white line across the wrist, painted on purpose.
One new handprint, the size of yours, still wet.

MURALS.name: The Hills
stages: The hideout's green hills at sunset, lamps in the windows.
The same hills at night, every window lit, a path down to the cave.
Under the hills, a dark shape like a sleeping animal curled around the cave mouth.
The sleeping shape's eye is half open, and it is looking at the lamps.

RELICS.name: Cracked seed-ark plaque
RELICS.text: A brass plaque: SEED ARK SEVEN. HOLD EVERYTHING UNTIL THE SKY IS KIND.

RELICS.name: Gardener's trowel
RELICS.text: Worn smooth. The handle is carved with a vine wrapped around a heart.

RELICS.name: Tether loom shuttle
RELICS.text: The Old Keepers wove tethers like cloth. This one still hums when you hold it near a creature.

RELICS.name: Withering ledger
RELICS.text: Columns of dead rivers and empty fields, then one line: WE GO DOWN TOMORROW.

RELICS.name: Seed sack
RELICS.text: Rough cloth, stamped with a number. Inside: forty different seeds, each wrapped and named.

RELICS.name: Planting roll
RELICS.text: A list of forty names under the heading THE PLANTING. Thirty-seven have a mark beside them: RETURNED.

RELICS.name: Forge coal
RELICS.text: Still warm after a hundred years. It burns with the same color as the Cinder Wyrm's breath.

RELICS.name: Pump valve
RELICS.text: Stamped DRY HALLS FOR THE SLEEPERS. The galleries were kept dry for someone.

RELICS.name: Gardener's wreath
RELICS.text: Iron leaves on an iron band. Not a crown. A gardener's wreath, worn by the one who keeps the song.

RELICS.name: Wind chime
RELICS.text: Five glass rods. Struck, it rings a scale that climbs, always upward. A way home by ear.

RELICS.name: Medicine label
RELICS.text: FOR ALL WHO SLEEP IN THE BLOOM, the label says. Creature and keeper are written in the same column.

RELICS.name: Choir tuning fork
RELICS.text: Struck, it plays the note the Choir has held for a hundred years.

RELICS.name: First singer's mask
RELICS.text: Inside, painted small: I SING SO IT DREAMS OF GARDENS.

RELICS.name: Second singer's mask
RELICS.text: Inside, scratched small: I AM TIRED. LET THE NEXT ONE SING.

RELICS.name: Lullaby sheet
RELICS.text: Sheet music with the words crossed out and rewritten: SLEEP, BUT NOT FOREVER.

RELICS.name: Sky map
RELICS.text: The surface as the Keepers last saw it: grey. Someone has painted it green, much later.

RELICS.name: Engine plate
RELICS.text: From the digging engine: DIG TO THE HEART. CUT NOTHING. LISTEN.

RELICS.name: Hybrid breeder's notes
RELICS.text: Three generations true and the Bloom stops pulling. It said so on the wall.

RELICS.name: Tether scar cast
RELICS.text: A plaster cast of a Keeper's wrist. The scar on it matches the one on your chest.

RELICS.name: Cradle song
RELICS.text: A child's song in the old letters. The tune is the one Ilsa's journal says her grandmother sang.

RELICS.name: Marrow family ring
RELICS.text: A ring with the Marrow crest. It is very, very old, and the crest is a singing mouth.

RELICS.name: Scribe's ink pot
RELICS.text: Dried violet ink. On the base, a scribe's mark: QUILL. Odile's family wrote for the Keepers.

RELICS.name: Ark seal
RELICS.text: Wax seal of the Ark: a seed inside a closed hand. The hand was meant to open one day.

RELICS.name: Returned Keeper's letter
RELICS.text: We came up. Three stayed. We swore not to speak of it, so the young would not go looking. Forgive us.

RELICS.name: Smith's tongs
RELICS.text: Marked with Brannoc's family stamp, three generations before his. His grandfather forged for the Keepers.

RELICS.name: Lantern lens
RELICS.text: A lens that catches no light until a Lumen creature breathes on it. Then it shows a garden under a blue sky.

RELICS.name: Root sample jar
RELICS.text: A root cut from Floor 7, sealed in glass a century ago. It is still growing, slowly, toward the jar's lid.

RELICS.name: Keeper's journal, first page
RELICS.text: Day one: the Bloom is planted. It loves the seeds already. I hope it will love letting them go.

RELICS.name: Keeper's journal, last page
RELICS.text: Year nine: it will not let go. It weeps when anything leaves. We must sing it to sleep before it learns to hold us too.

RELICS.name: Cut tether
RELICS.text: A tether cut cleanly at an extraction point, kept as proof that it could be done.

RELICS.name: Puffcap carving
RELICS.text: A little wooden Puffcap, worn by small hands. Biscuit's, maybe, or the Puffcap before her.

RELICS.name: Old Keeper's bell
RELICS.text: Rung at the end of every shift: one stroke for each Keeper who came back up that day.

RELICS.name: Unsent letter
RELICS.text: To my sister above: the sky you'll see is not the one I left. Plant something for me.

RELICS.name: Choir hymnal
RELICS.text: The song has words. Translated, they are not a spell. They are a lullaby, and the last verse promises a morning.

RELICS.name: Broken crown
RELICS.text: From the Hollow King: a real crown, not a wreath. He tried to rule it. It let him.

RELICS.name: Bloom seed
RELICS.text: A seed the size of a fist, dry and silent. Another ark, never planted. Kept in case.

RELICS.name: Third singer's chair leg
RELICS.text: Carved with names, one under another. The last two are Marrow, and Marrow.

RELICS.name: Heartwood splinter
RELICS.text: Warm. When you hold it, you hear your own heartbeat, and under it, a slower one.

RELICS.name: Morning verse
RELICS.text: The lullaby's lost last verse: AND WHEN THE SKY IS KIND, OPEN YOUR HAND.

RELICS.name: Ilsa's last pen
RELICS.text: Her pen, ink dried at the nib. She was writing to you.

MEMORIES.magmatitan: The Old Keepers fed their dead to the Abyss, as their custom was: give back to the garden. Something in the heat remembered their shapes and put them back together, wrong, out of rock and coal. It still carries a gardener's trowel welded into one fist.
MEMORIES.ashwyrm: It shed the Cinder Wyrm like a skin and went deeper, following the warmth of the old forge coals. It hoards them in its belly the way a child keeps warm stones. The Keepers' furnace went out the day it found the last one.
MEMORIES.drownedbloom: Mother Bloom's first daughter. When the pumps failed, she was left in the flooded galleries with nobody to turn toward. She grew toward the drip of the ceiling instead, and forgot what light was.
MEMORIES.pumpking: He ran the galleries' pumps for the Keepers for thirty years, and when they left he stayed with the machines. He still thinks it is his shift. Every pump in the galleries turns when he breathes.
MEMORIES.cantrix: The first singer. She sang the Bloom to sleep a hundred years ago, and her song became a body. Under the feathers of sound there is still a woman in a gardener's wreath, mouthing the words of a lullaby.
MEMORIES.hollowregent: Hollow kings come in threes. This one was the first king's steward, who kept the crown warm when the king went hollow. The Bloom liked how loyal he was, and kept him too.
MEMORIES.glassroc: The Storm Roc's mother, nesting at the top of the Spires where the wind is strongest. She built her nest from the Keepers' wind chimes, and they still ring a scale that climbs toward a sky she has never seen.
MEMORIES.mirrorqueen: Built from the shards of every crystal creature that fell in the Spires. Each shard remembers a different face, and she wears whichever one you hesitate to hit.
MEMORIES.sumpmother: Mother Bloom's second daughter, rotting and growing at once in the Sump. The Keepers' medicine leaked into her roots for a century. She has been trying to cure herself the whole time.
MEMORIES.blightwyrm: The Wyrm that swallowed the Keepers' medicine stores, every bottle at once. Half of it was poison and half was cure, and it has been both ever since.
MEMORIES.apothecarius: The Old Keepers' apothecary engine. Its last order was to cure the Bloom of its fear. It has spent a hundred years mixing doses for a patient the size of the world, and it is still not done.
MEMORIES.ilsa: Ilsa Marrow went down to keep the Bloom asleep in the Old Keepers' place, as the third singer of her family. The song has half-swallowed her. Break the song and she comes home; the Bloom will need a new answer.
MEMORIES.heart: Planted as an ark for a dying world, it loved everything it kept, and learned to fear everything that left. It never learned that the sky turned kind again. It is very old and very young at once, and it is listening.
MEMORIES.lord_hush: The silence between the Choir's verses, the breath the singers take, given a body. It hunts by sound because it was made of the absence of it, and every gunshot is a wound.
MEMORIES.lord_mirrorking: It wears the crowns of every king the Bloom remembers, and it hands your own strength back to you. It is what the Hollow King wanted to become: a ruler who only ever reflects.
MEMORIES.lord_thousand: A mother with a thousand children and no names for any of them. The Bloom made her to make sure nothing it loved would ever be alone. Everything near her is crowded and nobody is held.
MEMORIES.lord_shade: The Bloom watched every Keeper who came down. It learned you best. It is not cruel; it only wants to keep a copy, in case you leave too.

cindlet: A hopping spark that was born from the Abyss's last ember, small enough to sleep in a lantern.
Cut-free, it stops flickering. Cinderpups keep steady flames, as if they no longer need to prove they are alive.
Blazehounds were the Old Keepers' forge hounds, bred to carry coals between camps without burning the moss.
Infernox: the Keepers' ledgers call it 'the coal that walks'. It was the first creature they cut free, so the Abyss could be lit without the Bloom's permission.
pyrrox: A fox with a burning tail that it chases when it is happy.
Pyrrovex learn to set the tail down gently. Ilsa wrote that they 'stopped burning holes in the floor once they knew they were home'.
Flarefangs hunt in pairs, one to light, one to bite.
Solarix: a fox that carries a small sun. The Bloom grew the first one in the dark to remember what daylight looked like.
magmaul: A lava bear, slow and molten, that sleeps for weeks on warm stone.
Magmaw grows a crust it can crack at will, so it can hug without burning.
Calderon: the Abyss's oldest bear. Keepers built their camp on its back without knowing, and the scorch marks on Floor 3 are its footprints.
puffcap: A sturdy little mushroom that follows whoever feeds it. Ilsa's first companion, Biscuit, was a Puffcap.
Toadstools hum when they are content, a low sound the Bloom answers.
Sporelords seed the floors they walk on. Gardens follow them.
Mycoking: what a Puffcap becomes when nobody takes it home. Mother Bloom was almost one, once.
shroomite: A horned beetle with a toadstool shell, the Bloom's gardener.
Shroomhorns plough the moss so it grows evenly. They were the Keepers' farm animals.
Fungaroths guard the oldest mushroom beds and charge anything that steps on them.
Blightbeetle: the gardener that kept gardening after the gardeners left, until the garden grew teeth.
mycelisk: A serpent of living mycelium, woven out of the roots it slides through.
Hyphaserps can hear through every root they touch.
Rhizowyrm: one Rhizowyrm swallowed a Keeper forge coal and became the Cinder Wyrm. The rest stayed roots, listening to the whole Bloom at once.
dewdrip: A bouncy water droplet that the Bloom wrings from its ceilings.
Ripplets ride drips like falling stars.
Torrentails ran the Keepers' pumps for fun, pushing water uphill in loops.
Tsunamaw: the flood that rose in the galleries when the pumps failed, given a mouth. It is not angry. It is lonely for the pumps.
coralisk: A crab wearing a coral crown it grows itself.
Reefguards build walls of coral around anything small and wet.
Atollossus: an island that walks. The Keepers' sunken pump-house rests on one, and it has never put it down.
tidewyrm: A deep-water eel that sings under the water.
Deepwyrms carry air bubbles down for divers. Ilsa's Marrowtail did.
Maelstrix: Marrowtail went into the water after Ilsa and came back as the Leviathan. A cut-free Maelstrix is what Marrowtail might have been.
chirrup: A chattering cave flier that counts its friends out loud.
Chitterwings learn the songs of whatever they live near.
Screechlings can crack glass at fifty paces; the Spires' broken chimes are their work.
Banshriek: born in the Choir, it learned the singers' melody and wails it backwards, trying to wake them.
vesperbat: A big-eared bat that pulses in bursts, mapping rooms by echo.
Vespercalls answer each other across whole floors.
Nightvespers fly the Hollow Choir without light. The singers' song is their map.
Duskchorus: a whole flock that sings as one. The Keepers used them to carry the lullaby to the edges of the Bloom.
umbrowl: A shadow owl with a heavy cry.
Gloomhoots nest in the dark the Bloom makes when it sleeps deeply.
Eclipsowl: it watches the Heart's slow breathing from the Underheart's rafters and hoots once for every breath, keeping count for the singers.
zephling: A breezy fledgling that rides every draft it finds.
Zephyrins learn the wind lanes and teach them to the young.
Galewings fly the downdrafts of the Spires and then, impossibly, back up.
Tempestra: the Spires' wind always blows down, toward the heart. Tempestras are the only creatures that fly against it, and the Keepers followed them home.
kestrix: A razor-taloned hawk that dives from ledges.
Razorkests sharpen their talons on Keeper chimes.
Skyreavers have never seen a sky. They hunt the pale light of crystal ceilings instead.
Stormtalon: the Storm Roc's younger kin. Raised outside the Bloom, the first one flew straight up into a real sky and came back with rain on its feathers.
stormwing: A sky ray that rides thunderheads the Bloom grows in its high halls.
Thunderrays charge the air before every storm.
Cyclonox: the storm the Bloom dreams when it dreams of weather. Cut free, it rains on the hideout's garden on purpose.
shardling: A chip off a bigger gem. Every crystal creature on the upper floors was shed by the Matriarch.
Facetlings turn toward any light like flowers.
Prismhearts beat. The Keepers called them 'the Bloom's spare hearts'.
Diamantine: the Matriarch shed it to wander up toward the light because she could not. Every Diamantine that reaches the surface carries her a little closer.
prismoth: Lumimoths gather at extraction points, where the tether thins and the light leaks in.
Spectramoths paint rainbows on cave walls. Some of the oldest murals are theirs, not the Keepers'.
Auroramoth: the Keepers bred them to remember what a sunrise looked like, and to show it to the Bloom.
geodon: A tortoise carrying a geode, slow and patient.
Amethortoises grow their shells a ring a year; the oldest have a hundred.
Gemcitadel: the Keepers built their archive inside a living Gemcitadel, so the records would outlast them. It is still walking around somewhere below the Spires.
pebblet: A pebble that rolls everywhere, mostly downhill.
Rollstones roll uphill when they are happy, which is unsettling.
Boulderlings block doors for their friends.
Avalanchion: the rockslide that sealed the old Keeper camp, when the Keepers left. It has been guarding the door from the inside ever since.
bastion: A living fortress wall that the Bloom puts in front of anything it wants to keep.
Bulwarks stand in doorways for days without moving.
Citadelion: the Bloom grew it to keep the Keepers in. Cut free, it keeps the hideout's gate, and lets everyone through.
monolord: A floating monolith with a crown.
Obelords carve runes on their own sides in the old Keeper alphabet, though nobody taught them.
Pantheon: a temple that walks. The words on it are the Keepers' lullaby, and Monolord lines sing it when the Bloom stirs.
toxlet: A bog newt with a dripping frill, born in the Sump.
Toxfrills flare their frills to warn, not to poison.
Blightnewts eat the Sump's rot and make medicine of it.
Plaguewyrm: the Sump's poison and the Keepers' cure in one body. Its venom, diluted, is the Apothecary's best serum.
fangmire: A coiled marsh serpent whose fangs glow green.
Venomcoils guard the Keepers' medicine bottles as if they were eggs.
Basilurk: the Keepers' records name it the Apothecary's familiar. It tested every cure on itself first.
hydravine: A three-headed vine hydra from the deep Sump. The heads argue.
Hydrabloom: three heads, three voices, one song. Sorrel thinks the Bloom grew it to practice singing with itself.
glimmet: A lantern moth that drinks the dark.
Lanternmoth: the Underheart's only light came from them, and the singers sang by it for a hundred years.
halowing: A ringed seraph-bird that hums at dawn, though it has never seen one.
Haloseraph: the first singer's companion. It still hums the lullaby's lost last verse, the one about the morning.
solaryx: A sun-maned beast from the Underheart's deepest hall.
Solarch: the Bloom grew it from its memory of the sun on the day it was planted. Bring one home and it will stand on the hill at dawn, comparing.
blazewing: Two tethers braided into one: Ember and Gale. The Bloom cannot hold a creature it did not plan.
Phoenixwing: a fire that flies. Hybrids like it convinced Sorrel that the Bloom is one organism, because only one organism could be confused by them.
bogbloom: Tide and Fungal braided together; a marsh that walks.
Mirelord: it grows a garden wherever it sits down. The Keepers tried to breed one on purpose and never could.
resonyx: Crystal and Echo; it rings like a struck glass.
Harmonyx: tuned to the Choir's note. When it sings, the singers below sing quieter.
forgeheart: Warden and Ember; a hearth with legs.
Anvilheart: Brannoc swears his grandfather's forge was built around one.
squallfin: Gale and Tide; it swims through the air.
Stormfin: rain falls up around it.
duskcap: Fungal and Echo; a mushroom that whispers back.
Nightbloom: it opens only in the dark and repeats what it heard there.
gemguard: Crystal and Warden; a wall that glitters.
Jewelward: the Archive's vault door was one, once.
steamfin: Ember and Tide; it travels in its own fog.
Steamfin Ascendant: the Keepers' pumps ran on steam from these.
kilnspark: Ember and Crystal; it fires glass from sand.
Kilnspark Ascendant: the chimes of the Spires were blown by one.
mossguard: Fungal and Warden; a hedge that stands guard.
Mossguard Ascendant: it grows over graves to keep them quiet.
deepsinger: Tide and Echo; it sings under the water.
Deepsinger Ascendant: it knows the lullaby's middle verse, the one about the sea.
glasswing: Gale and Crystal; its wings are panes.
Glasswing Ascendant: through its wings, the cave ceiling looks like sky.
wailwind: Gale and Echo; a howl that blows.
Wailwind Ascendant: the wind in the Spires is one, sleeping.
blightcap: Venom and Fungal; poison that grows.
Blightcap Ascendant: it rots what is dead and leaves the living alone.
mirefang: Venom and Tide; a bite from the water.
Mirefang Ascendant: the Sump's drains were dug by them.
dawnsong: Lumen and Echo; it hums the color of morning.
Dawnsong Ascendant: it sings the lullaby's last verse aloud, and the Bloom stirs.
prismheart: Lumen and Crystal; a lantern grown from a gem.
Prismheart Ascendant: it holds light for days after the light is gone.
eclipsar: Venom and Lumen, a pairing written only on a rune wall in the Sump: VENOM WED TO LIGHT MAKES AN ECLIPSE.
Eclipsar Ascendant: light and poison in one body. The Keepers called it the cure for fear, and never managed to breed it.

brannoc.text: Reach Floor 5, deep in a vein.
brannoc.done: That coal in the Wyrm's belly? Keeper-forged. My grandfather's mark is on every old blade down there. He wasn't just a smith. He was one of them.

brannoc.text: Have 8 Old Keeper relics read in the Archive.
brannoc.done: Forty went down. Thirty-seven came back and swore never to talk about it. My family kept the forge lit for the three who didn't. Now I know why we never let it go out.
She's home. I'll forge her a new pen. Steel this time, so it won't dry out.

pip.text: Copy 4 rune walls in the Bloom.
pip.done: I mapped every floor, but I never could read the walls. You can. Pip's map, page two: the walls aren't decoration, they're directions.
Floor seven isn't on any map because it isn't a floor. It's a body. I'm going to need a bigger notebook. And a smaller pencil, so it doesn't notice.
She left these for you, not me. That's fine. She always said I'd lose them. I'd have lost them.

sorrel.done: Hybrids! Two tethers braided into one, and the Bloom can't hold either. Only one organism could be confused like that. I'm sure now: it's all one creature.

sorrel.text: Raise a creature of Generation 3 or later.
sorrel.done: Bred true three times and the Bloom lets go. The Old Keepers knew it. They wrote it on a wall, and then they forgot to tell anyone.

sorrel.text: Choose an ending at the Heart.
sorrel.done: Whatever you chose, write it down. Somebody after you will need to know what the Bloom was, and what you did about it.

odile.name: Odile Quill
odile.arriveText: Arrives when you first reach the veins on Floor 4.
odile.intro: Odile Quill. I read dead languages for a living, and the Bloom is written in one. Bring me relics and I'll read one every few days. A Lumen in the Archive reads faster than I do, and I won't be offended.
idle: Runes are just letters wearing a disguise. Count which shape turns up most. It's probably E.
Every wall down there was carved by someone who wanted it read. That's the kindest kind of writing.
My family wrote for the Keepers. I found our mark on an ink pot from the Abyss.
If two words share a shape at the same spot, they share a letter. That's the whole trick.

quests.done: Same alphabet on both, and the same hand. The Keepers didn't scribble. They published.

quests.text: Have 3 relics read in the Archive.
quests.done: SEED ARK SEVEN. It's an ark. They didn't dig the Bloom. They planted it, to carry the world through something called the Withering.
Six floors of camps and pumps and chimes. They meant to come and go for generations. Something made them stop.

quests.text: Have 12 relics read in the Archive.
quests.done: My family's mark, on an ink pot from the deep. Quills wrote the Keepers' ledgers. We came back up with the thirty-seven, and we kept their secret so well we forgot it.
THREE STAYED BELOW. THE THIRD SINGER WAS MARROW. You know what that means. You've known since the first wall, I think.

odile.outro: Every wall is read. I'll keep the Archive open for whoever comes after you. They'll need a head start.

hesper.name: Hesper Wick
hesper.arriveText: Arrives when you first reach Floor 5.
hesper.intro: Hesper Wick. I patch up creatures, and Keepers when they let me. I came for the Old Keepers' medicine stores. Turns out they only ever wrote labels for creatures.
idle: Every creature born in the Bloom has a tether. I've stitched a thousand of them. Never seen one on a person. Not yet.
Venom's just medicine at the wrong dose.
The Sump is a pharmacy that forgot its own labels.
Rest your creatures. The Bloom never sleeps properly, and neither do they after a raid.

quests.done: Ten extractions, ten clean cuts. The Keepers called extraction points 'the doors'. They thought of the Bloom as a house.
The roots down there have a pulse. One pulse. I've only ever felt that in a single body. Sorrel's going to be insufferable.

quests.text: Copy the rune wall WE TOO CARRY THE THREAD on Floor 7, then copy 10 walls in all.
quests.done: We too carry the thread. Keeper, I need you to look at your own chest. There. That thin white line. You've always had it, haven't you?

quests.text: Have 20 relics read in the Archive.
quests.done: The medicine labels said FOR ALL WHO SLEEP IN THE BLOOM. Creature and Keeper, same column. People were in the ark too. We're what came out.
She's thin and she hums in her sleep, but her thread is quiet. Whatever you do at the Heart, she'll live through it. I'll make sure.

hesper.outro: Nobody's thread pulls anymore. I'm almost out of work. Almost.

rowan.name: Rowan Marrow
rowan.arriveText: Arrives when you first reach the Underheart on Floor 7.
rowan.intro: Rowan Marrow. Ilsa's brother. I heard someone reached the Underheart, and I couldn't sit at home anymore. I never had the knack for the Bloom. She did. Our grandmother did.
idle: Grandmother used to sing us a song with no words. I hum it when I can't sleep.
Ilsa wrote you a letter, didn't she. She always wrote to strangers better than to family.
We all have the scar. Mother said it was a burn. Everybody's mother said it was a burn.
If you find her, tell her the garden's still growing. She'll want to know.

quests.done: Floor eight. She went past this. Tell me there are signs of her. Even a page.
'A Marrow sang here before me.' Our grandmother. She went 'to the hills' when I was six and never came back. Ilsa knew. She went to take her place.
You heard her? Singing? Then she's alive. Half of her, anyway. That's more than we had yesterday.
She's home. She asked about the garden first. Of course she did. Thank you. I don't know how to say it better than that.

quests.text: Choose an ending at the Heart.
quests.done: Ilsa says no Marrow will ever have to sing down there again. Whatever you chose, you chose it awake. That's all she asked.

rowan.outro: The Marrows owe you a garden. Pick a plot. Any plot.
